title: U.K. sanctions Israeli companies involved in building illegal settlements in West Bank

Britain said on Tuesday it would impose sanctions on eight Israeli construction companies involved in building settlements in the occupied West Bank, as part of its effort to protect the idea of a two-state solution.
Britain says newly imposed sanctions to disrupt firms' access to finance, support for more construction

Britain said on Tuesday it would impose sanctions on eight Israeli construction companies involved in building settlements in the occupied West Bank, as well as on an activist group responsible for blocking aid to Gaza.

The firms targeted for asset freezes and director disqualifications include Har Hevron Development Company, Hemdat Shomron and S.A.G. (Velvel) Construction and Development, which build and develop homes in the West Bank.

The government announced the sanctions package shortly before the final deadlines for the E1 tender, a settlement project that would bisect the Israeli-occupied West Bank and cut it off from East Jerusalem, fragmenting the land that Palestinians hope will form the heart of a state.

"Protecting the two-state solution is the North Star of this government's approach," British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said in a statement. "That is why my message on E1 is clear: Do not bid, do not build and do not profit from the destruction of the two-state solution."

Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar said the sanctions were a "hostile act targeting private, law-abiding companies," adding that the Israeli government would consider new ways to strengthen settlements in the West Bank.

"Israel will respond to the British government’s actions with countermeasures. A wide range of possible responses is currently under consideration. Our decisions will be announced in due course," he said in a post on X.
Israel pushes into West Bank for settlement expansion

Saar remains foreign minister in a caretaker government led by Benjamin Netanyahu. An Oct. 27 election stripped Netanyahu's coalition of its parliamentary majority but no winner emerged, and talks are ongoing to form a new government.
The Palestinian Authority welcomed the British sanctions and called for other countries to take similar action.
Deteriorated U.K.-Israel relationship
The sanctions are the latest in a series of measures by Britain targeting the settlement policy and underscore Israel's growing diplomatic isolation among some traditional allies.

Britain's relationship with Israel has deteriorated significantly over the past three years because of disagreements over the way that Israel has conducted its war against Hamas and the Israeli government's plans to expand settlements in the occupied West Bank.
Israel in September threatened to close the British Consulate building in East Jerusalem in response to London’s decision to impose trade sanctions on Israeli settlements in the West Bank.
British and Israeli diplomats last month reached a last-minute agreement to avoid the closure of the consulate.
Palestinian farmers risk their lives to pick their olives

Britain joined several other countries including Canada in 2025 in recognizing a Palestinian state as a means of advancing the two-state solution, and in September announced plans to block imports from Israeli settlements in the West Bank.

Last year, Britain also imposed sanctions on two far-right Israeli cabinet ministers, Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich, accusing them of repeatedly inciting violence against Palestinians in the West Bank.

While those measures were co-ordinated with international partners, Britain acted alone on Tuesday in sanctioning the Israeli companies, saying the move would disrupt their access to finance and support for further construction in the West Bank.
Israeli group obstructing Gaza aid sanctioned

As part of the measures announced on Tuesday, the government also imposed sanctions on Tzav 9, an Israeli activist group that it said had regularly blocked humanitarian aid trucks delivering food, water and fuel to the Gaza Strip. The new sanctions placed include an asset freeze and director disqualification, which prevent sanctioned individuals from using corporate structures to operate or raise funds.

In June 2024, the U.S. State Department under the Biden administration sanctioned Tzav 9, which it described as a "violent extremist Israeli group." The European Union followed suit a month later by also imposing sanctions on the group under its Global Human Rights Sanctions Regime.

According to the United Nations, over 150,000 tents and 300,000 tarpaulins that humanitarian partners and donors purchased are outside Gaza, ready to go in, but are being held by the Israeli authorities, the U.K. said in its statement, adding that the Israeli authorities also continue to block timber from entering, leaving no emergency shelter kits available in Gaza.

"We are suffering a lot here in Gaza because of the lack of tents and the lack of sheltering equipment that the Israelis are putting restrictions on," Mohammed Salha, general director of the Palestinian NGO Network in Gaza, told CBC News on Tuesday.
Israel's military agency that co-ordinates aid, COGAT, says it has a proactive "winterization plan" and that supplies and medicines continue to enter Gaza.
With files from CBC News
